explanation_bullets: A mutual fund exit load is a fee charged to investors when they withdraw or redeem their units from a mutual fund scheme.
The exit load is typically a percentage of the withdrawal amount or the net asset value (NAV) of the units being redeemed.
The primary purpose of an exit load is to deter investors from withdrawing their money quickly, allowing the fund manager to maintain a stable portfolio.
Exit loads are usually applicable for a specific period, such as within a year of investment, and may vary depending on the type of mutual fund scheme.
The exit load is deducted from the redemption proceeds and the remaining amount is paid to the investor.
The details of the exit load, including the percentage and applicable period, are disclosed in the mutual fund scheme's offer document and key information memorandum.
A brokerage fee is a charge levied by a broker or brokerage firm for their services.
The fee is typically a percentage of the transaction value or a flat rate per transaction.
Brokerage fees can vary depending on the type of investment, such as stocks, bonds, or mutual funds.
These fees are usually deducted from the investor's account at the time of transaction.
Brokerage fees can be negotiable, and some firms may offer discounted rates for frequent traders or high-volume investors.
The fees are a source of revenue for brokerage firms, covering their operational costs and profit margins.
